A fake needs a >=48-slot vtable; every add_* must hand back an EventRegistrationToken (out param) and the host must keep the handler.

IUIElement (IID 676d0be9-b65c-41c6-ba40-58cf87f201c1 @0x2de660) must also implement get_RenderSize (slot 23, +0x5c; helper 0x1daa58): AttachToPanel 0x1da634 reads the panel RenderSize twice (width/height x platform scale) and passes them to client vtable+0x50 setSize; 0 makes setSize fall back to 240x140 (0x59776/0x5977c). panel_requirements lists only Visibility (slot 22).

Event delegates: handlers passed to add_* are C++/CX delegate objects (e.g. SizeChangedEventHandler built by 0x1dcc5c with three vtables at +0/+4/+8, lambda 0x1df809). The host must QI the delegate for its delegate IID and call Invoke(sender,args) (slot 3); SizeChangedEventArgs must provide get_NewSize at slot 7 (+0x1c) returning Size{float,float} (0x1df84a, and four calls in 0x1da32c). Same for CompositionScaleChanged, DpiChanged, OrientationChanged, VisibilityChanged (args slot 6 get_Visible), InputPane Showing/Hiding, BackPressed. Not spelled out by the finder.

Ordering hazard around the first SizeChanged: OnWindowSizeChanged 0x1da32c calls client->vf20 setSize (vtable+0x50, blx at 0x1da3ac) without testing AppMain+0x3c; setSize -> 0x586ec -> App::vf8 -> client+0xC, which the init worker stores only at 0x471f4 (runInit). Raising SizeChanged before the worker has started faults at 0x58718, and a SizeChanged during Minecraft::init mutates client+0x20/+0x24 and the GUI-scale globals concurrently with init. The finder's instruction 'raise SizeChanged exactly once right after construction' is unsafe as stated: wait for client+0xC != NULL (or AppMain+0x3c==1) first, but still deliver SizeChanged BEFORE the first Tick-driven AttachToPanel, because ApplyResolutionOverride (inside SetSwapChainPanel) halves DR+0x60/+0x64, which AppPlatform_Winrt::initialize 0x4b55c later copies into platform+0x3c/+0x40.

AttachToPanel / AppPlatform_Winrt::initialize 0x4b55c (HID::Initialize, DisplayInformation, CoreWindow, EditBox/Button handling) is still undecoded; the Tick cannot complete (and the render loop never starts) until every WinRT call in it is faked. Window::Current (0x1dac80) and IWindow.get_CoreWindow (0x1daacc, slot 10) are required.

ThreadPool fake contract: IThreadPoolStatics (b6bf67dd-...) slot 6 RunAsync(handler,&op) for the init job (0x1da52e) and slot 8 RunWithPriorityAndOptionsAsync(handler,prio,opts,&op) for the render loop (High, TimeSliced). The work-item handler receives the returned IAsyncAction as its argument and reads IAsyncInfo.get_Status (slot 7) through QI IID 00000036: it must read 0 (Started) until Cancel (slot 9), then Canceled(2). The init job must run on a real thread (seconds of shader compilation) and must have STARTED before SizeChanged (see above).

FL 9_1 runtime limits behind the '9_3' lie are unexamined (only shader compilation was tested): texture size (9_1 2048 vs 9_3 4096; the probe PC cannot prove it), number of render targets, primitive-count/index limits (mce::Buffer::BindBuffer 0xc669c via sub_c6bd4 maps index element size 4 -> DXGI_FORMAT_R32_UINT (0x2a), 2 -> R16_UINT (0x39); whether the game binds 32-bit index buffers or draws >65535 primitives is not determined), anisotropic filtering, occlusion queries, depth-clip, non-power-of-two rules (the game rounds to pow2 only via d8e4c).

Real-hardware items still open (Tegra/Surface RT): dcomp.dll availability for presentation path A; whether FLIP_SEQUENTIAL + DXGI_SCALING_STRETCH is accepted by CreateSwapChainForHwnd on Win 8.1/RT; whether the Tegra driver accepts the level_9_1 blobs (only a desktop driver/WARP forced to {9_1} was tested, by the finder and by me).

Shader source delivery: loadShader 0xd65cc reads 'shaders/dx11/<name>.hlsl' through the AppPlatform reader at [0xddd7e0] vtable+0x38 (another area) and also accepts an inline source (branch on sub_127180); that reader must resolve the path relative to the package 'data' folder. D3DCompile then gets pSourceName 'data/shaders/dx11/<name>.hlsl' and resolves ShaderConstants.fxh relative to the process cwd (reproduced), so SetCurrentDirectory(game root) or an ID3DInclude hook is mandatory.

HandleDeviceLost / ValidateDevice would re-enter the D3D11CreateDevice hook and rebuild only DR objects (AppMain's IDeviceNotify is empty); the host hook and fake dispatcher must tolerate that or the host must treat DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED/RESET from Present as fatal. Present(0,0) on a flip chain has no waitable object; throttling relies on SetMaximumFrameLatency(1). On an HWND chain with an occluded/minimised window Present returns DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED (success) so the render thread would spin.

createApp 0x1d9dd4 (init-time, not frame) also needs ApplicationData.Current.LocalFolder.Path and Package.Current.InstalledLocation.Path (0x1dab28/0x1dad20/0x4ea38); AppMain+0x30 is a float set in the ctor (0x1d9d7c) and +0x34/+0x38/+0x3c are written by createApp (client, platform holder cell, ready byte). Not covered by this area but required before the first frame.
